$comment: Point COUNCIL_CONFIG at this file, or drop it at ~/.config/model-council/config.json
where the server finds it automatically. Declare each endpoint once under
'providers', then list the models you want on the council under 'members'.
${ENV_VAR} is expanded from the environment, so this file can be shared or
committed without the keys in it.
$comment2: timeout, retries, retry_backoff and proxy may also be set at the top level,
as the default every provider and member inherits. These are the built-in
values; 'proxy' is left out here, which means every member follows whatever
HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY this machine sets. Set it to false to send the whole
council straight out instead, or to a URL to put it behind one proxy — and
either way a single provider or member can still choose its own route.

internal.$comment: an endpoint your machine's proxy cannot reach — go direct

$comment: 'weight' is how far this member's opinion carries against the others.
Default 1, max 10, 0 = advisory only. It changes nothing about the call:
ask_all reports it with the answers, whenever the council's weights differ.
members.label: GPT-5

$comment: 'vision': false for a model that cannot be shown an image. It then sits
out any call carrying one in 'materials', rather than answering about the
text alone in the same confident register as the members who saw it.
'cache' is the other half: material is marked as a cacheable prefix on the
anthropic format, and this turns that off for a gateway that rejects the
field. It may also be set once on the provider.
a member may skip 'provider' and carry its own connection — and its own
route: this one is the only seat that needs a proxy, so it names one
rather than the council doing it for everybody. 'direct' is the opposite
move (see the 'internal' provider above), and both are printed by

members.$comment: a member you would rather have fail fast than retry for minutes
